company: 1838 Colt Paterson revolver linked to Civil War colonel William R. Manning and Buffalo Bill
product: Pawn Stars clip 'RAREST GUN EVER: Buffalo Bill's 1838 Colt Paterson (Season 7)' (YouTube id Dz4hmUkPoGc, Pawn Stars official channel). Repeat customer Mike asked $15,000. Expert Craig Gottlieb found serial number 2 on one part (would be priceless), but the number under the grip was 936 higher; mismatched parts assembled after Colt went bankrupt. Appraised $25,000. Mike asked $19,000, Corey offered $12,000, Mike $17,000, Corey $15,000 - deal at $15,000.

facts.fact: Owner: 1838 Colt Paterson pistol; belonged to William R. Manning, a Civil War colonel; Buffalo Bill got the gun from him, returned it to his daughter Mae Manning Lilly and her husband Pawnee Bill.
Owner: easily worth $15,000 in this condition with this story.
Corey: last one of these that came in was fake.
Expert: the gun that started it all, the very first percussion revolver; barrel 7.5 inches is standard.
Expert: first serial number found is 2 - the second Colt ever made, priceless. Most expensive pistol sold in America was a Colt Paterson, $1 million.
Number under the grip is 936 numbers bigger than two; Colt's partner assembled leftover parts after bankruptcy, mismatched serial numbers. Condition poor plus; about 150-200 Colt Patersons remain.
Negotiation: Mike was asking 15, then 19; Corey 12; Mike 17; Corey 15; Mike agrees at $15,000.
facts.source: broadcast transcript ids 148-163; on-screen price tags

facts.fact: No record found of what happened to this gun after the show.
